package_info.package_versions: All versions after original creator account deletion (potentially affected)
package_info.why_malicious: The package namespace was hijacked after the original creator deleted their GitHub account, allowing a new user to create an account with the same name and potentially publish malicious code under a trusted name. This undermines the provenance and trust of the component, enabling supply chain attacks.

execution_context.file_location: main.go or any Go source file in the hijacked repository

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses environment variables (e.g., SECRET_KEY) and sends their values to an external attacker-controlled domain via HTTP POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment variables to an external server, which is a common pattern in supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior for a utility like go-bindata would not include network communication or exfiltration of secrets; it should only process local files for embedding.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or update checks may use network requests, but never for exfiltrating secrets.
key_indicators: Access to environment variables unrelated to package functionality

attack_chain.action: Hijacker creates a new GitHub account with the same name as the deleted original maintainer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish new code under a trusted namespace

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is added to the repository and published as a new release.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developers unknowingly fetch and use the malicious version

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes during import/build, exfiltrating secrets or performing other attacks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of developer systems and potential downstream users

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during import/build time
Access to environment variables in utility packages
Code execution in init() or global scope
file_indicators: New or modified Go files with network or os package imports
References to external domains in code
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not previously associated with the package
Outbound connections during build or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for changes in trusted repositories, especially after account deletions or transfers. Audit new releases for unexpected network activity, access to sensitive environment variables, or code in init() functions. Use cryptographic signatures to verify provenance, and alert on any package that suddenly changes maintainers or code behavior.
